input_signals.name: SelfFinancedProfitPower
input_signals.hypothesis: Current operating profitability is valuable only if the firm's balance sheet shows that past profits were retained rather than distributed or offset by borrowing; retained earnings relative to total obligations measures whether profitability has historically been self-financing rather than debt-supported.
input_signals.reasoning: The multiplicative form makes leverage genuinely conditioning rather than additive — a highly levered firm with negative or thin retained earnings collapses the signal regardless of its current ROA, which is exactly the "levered versus durable profitability" distinction the previous rank sum failed to implement. Retained-earnings-to-liabilities is a stock measure of cumulative internal funding, so it captures financing quality with information not already spanned by a static debt-to-assets sort.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( ind_rank( ratio( oiadp, at ) ), ind_rank( ratio( re, lt ) ) )

input_signals.name: WorkingCapitalLightProfit
input_signals.hypothesis: Operating profits generated with little net working capital per dollar of sales are cash profits; the same margins earned while tying up receivables and inventory represent accrual-heavy profitability that decays.
input_signals.reasoning: This repairs the earlier flagged construction, whose working-capital trend leg carried a documented opposite-sign loading, by using the level of working-capital intensity with the correct (negative) orientation and dropping the coverage-costly five-year trend. The multiplicative form makes operating-cycle efficiency a conditioner on profitability rather than an independent additive bet.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( ind_rank( ratio( oiadp, at ) ), ind_rank( neg( ratio( sub( act, lct ), sale ) ) ) )

input_signals.name: DeleveragingProfitability
input_signals.hypothesis: High profitability accompanied by falling debt intensity signals internally funded operating strength, while high profitability accompanied by rising debt intensity signals returns that are being manufactured or sustained by new borrowing and are therefore fragile.
input_signals.reasoning: This changes the channel from a static leverage level (already priced) to the direction of financing policy, which is a flow variable that markets update slowly and that separates self-funding from debt-funded profitability. A one-year change keeps coverage high while still identifying the financing dynamic.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( ind_rank( ratio( oiadp, at ) ), ind_rank( neg( delta( ratio( add( dltt, dlc ), at ), 1 ) ) ) )

input_signals.name: StableCapitalStructureProfit
input_signals.hypothesis: Durable operating strength shows up as profitability sustained without repeatedly re-engineering the balance sheet; volatile liability-to-asset ratios reveal firms whose reported returns depend on episodic financing, restructuring, or off-and-on distress management.
input_signals.reasoning: The stability channel here is financing-policy stability rather than the heavily mined earnings-volatility channel, so it is distinguishable from the QMJ earnings-stability leg while still testing the "stable and financially healthy" part of the economic story. A three-year window is the shortest that can measure dispersion, chosen deliberately to avoid the coverage collapse seen with five-year operators.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( ind_rank( ma( ratio( oiadp, at ), 3 ) ), ind_rank( neg( vol( ratio( lt, at ), 3 ) ) ) )

input_signals.name: RolloverRiskAdjustedProfit
input_signals.hypothesis: Reported operating profitability is durable only when the firm is not exposed to near-term refinancing pressure; debt maturing within a year that exceeds the firm's liquid asset base forces asset sales, cost cuts, or dilutive financing that destroy the profit stream regardless of how strong current returns look.
input_signals.reasoning: Unlike the flagged version, the conditioning leg contains no profitability variable at all — dlc/act is a pure maturity-structure and liquidity measure, so it is close to orthogonal to ROA and cannot collapse into a re-scaled profitability sort. The mechanism is rollover risk rather than solvency level, which is a distinct channel from the archive's profit-to-liabilities composites and gives the short leg genuine content: highly profitable but liquidity-strained firms.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( ind_rank( ratio( oiadp, at ) ), ind_rank( neg( ratio( dlc, act ) ) ) )

input_signals.name: IntangibleProfitWithSlack
input_signals.hypothesis: True operating strength includes profits that are currently being expensed away as intangible investment, and it is durable only when the firm holds enough liquid resources relative to current obligations to keep funding that investment through downturns rather than cutting it to service near-term claims.
input_signals.reasoning: This abandons the "profit divided by a liability stock" family entirely: the profitability leg is R&D-adjusted operating income (treating unreported R&D as zero, the standard convention), and the quality leg is a pure liquidity-buffer ratio containing no earnings variable, so the two legs are economically and statistically distinct. The interaction tests whether the market underprices intangible-intensive profitability specifically when the balance sheet can sustain the investment, which is a different mechanism from leverage or solvency conditioning already in the archive.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( ind_rank( ratio( add( oiadp, coalesce( xrd, 0 ) ), at ) ), ind_rank( ratio( act, lct ) ) )

input_signals.name: ShortDebtShareProfit
input_signals.hypothesis: Profitability is fragile when the firm's obligations are concentrated at the short end of the maturity spectrum, because refinancing must be negotiated repeatedly and is withdrawn exactly in bad states; maturity structure, not leverage level, is the financial-health dimension that conditions durable profits.
input_signals.reasoning: The strongest archive signal used dlc/act, which mixes maturity concentration with liquidity; this strips out the liquid-asset denominator and keeps only the maturity-structure content, scaled by total obligations so zero-debt firms remain in the sample at the favorable end. Because leverage *levels* have repeatedly failed while this dlc-based signal succeeded, separating maturity risk from liquidity is the highest-information decomposition available.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( ind_rank( ratio( oiadp, at ) ), ind_rank( neg( ratio( dlc, lt ) ) ) )

input_signals.name: IntangibleProfitLowLeverage
input_signals.hypothesis: Profitability measured inclusive of expensed R&D captures true operating strength that accounting understates, and such intangible-rich earnings are only defensible when the firm is not obliged to service a large liability stock that competes with continued investment.
input_signals.reasoning: This is the diagnostic counterpart to the archive's IntangibleProfitWithSlack: it keeps the R&D-adjusted profitability leg but swaps the liquidity conditioner for a plain leverage conditioner, so a strong result would attribute that signal's alpha to the intangible add-back while a weak result would attribute it to the liquidity leg. Given every previous leverage-level conditioner failed, this is a clean attribution test rather than a hopeful restatement.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( ind_rank( ratio( add( oiadp, coalesce( xrd, 0 ) ), at ) ), ind_rank( neg( ratio( lt, at ) ) ) )

input_signals.name: PayableStretchProfit
input_signals.hypothesis: Operating current liabilities net of debt are supplier and accrual financing; a profitable firm that stretches these balances relative to its cost of goods is quietly funding operations off its trade partners, a low-visibility form of liquidity strain that precedes profit reversal.
input_signals.reasoning: The archive shows lct/at is weak while dlc/lt is strong, which leaves open whether the non-debt part of current liabilities is neutral or actively harmful — this signal isolates exactly that residual and scales it by cost of goods so it reads as a payables-days measure rather than a size ratio. It also directly reconciles the one negative-alpha result in the archive, whose long leg loaded on high current liabilities relative to sales.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( ind_rank( ratio( oiadp, at ) ), ind_rank( neg( ratio( sub( lct, dlc ), cogs ) ) ) )

input_signals.name: ShrinkingRolloverExposure
input_signals.hypothesis: A profitable firm that is actively retiring the short-maturity portion of its debt is converting operating strength into financial resilience, while one whose short-term borrowing is rising is funding current operations with the most fragile form of capital even as reported profits look healthy.
input_signals.reasoning: Total-debt changes failed in this archive (α=0.6%) while the level of short-term debt succeeded, so the untested question is whether the *change* in the specifically fragile liability class carries information that the change in aggregate debt does not. It is a cheap and highly diagnostic test: a strong result would say the market prices refinancing-exposure news, a null would confirm that only the level of rollover risk matters.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( ind_rank( ratio( oiadp, at ) ), ind_rank( neg( delta( ratio( dlc, at ), 1 ) ) ) )

input_signals.name: StableFundingProfit
input_signals.hypothesis: Persistent profitability combined with a stable, unchanging short-term funding position identifies firms that finance themselves the same way through good and bad years; firms whose rollover exposure swings are opportunistic borrowers whose profits depend on continuously accommodating credit conditions.
input_signals.reasoning: The earlier stability attempt applied volatility to total leverage — a variable that carries no alpha in this archive — so this applies the same stability concept to the one funding variable that demonstrably does, which is a substantive relocation of the mechanism rather than a re-parameterization. Smoothing profitability over three years simultaneously tests whether persistence in the profitability leg adds to the interaction, at a modest coverage cost.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( ind_rank( ma( ratio( oiadp, at ), 3 ) ), ind_rank( neg( vol( ratio( dlc, act ), 3 ) ) ) )

input_signals.name: NearTermChargeCoverage
input_signals.hypothesis: What determines whether profits survive is the ratio of the cash the business throws off each year to the cash it must produce within the year — maturing debt plus interest — so profitability paired with high coverage of near-term fixed charges is the sharpest separation of durable from fragile earnings.
input_signals.reasoning: Every strong archive conditioner compares maturing claims to a *stock* of liquid assets; this replaces the stock with the annual cash profit flow, which is the resource that actually retires those claims and which asset-light or fast-turning firms possess in abundance despite thin balance sheets. Coverage should stay reasonable because the denominator is nonzero for nearly all levered firms, and the industry ranking limits distortion from the small group with negligible short-term charges.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( ind_rank( ratio( oiadp, at ) ), ind_rank( ratio( oibdp, add( dlc, xint ) ) ) )

input_signals.name: PeakRolloverExposureProfit
input_signals.hypothesis: Fiscal-year-end short-term debt understates true refinancing exposure because firms pay down revolvers before the balance-sheet date; the highest short-term-debt-to-liquid-assets ratio observed over the last three annual reports is a better measure of the funding pressure a profitable firm actually operates under, and profits earned without ever hitting a stressed funding state are the durable ones.
input_signals.reasoning: This is not a crossing of two tested legs: it changes the measurement claim about the conditioner itself — worst-case rather than point-in-time rollover exposure — which is an identifiable statement about window dressing and reporting-date bias rather than a re-labelling of an existing signal. It is also distinct from the accepted volatility version, since a firm can have stable-but-persistently-high exposure (penalized here, unpenalized by VOL) or a single stressed year (penalized here, rewarded by a low current level).
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( ind_rank( ratio( oiadp, at ) ), ind_rank( neg( ts_max( ratio( dlc, act ), 3 ) ) ) )

input_signals.name: ConservativeDepreciationProfit
input_signals.hypothesis: A firm that reports high operating profitability while charging an aggressive depreciation rate against its long-lived asset base is understating its true earnings power; conservative accounting policy is therefore a quality marker that separates genuinely productive assets from profits flattered by stretched useful lives.
input_signals.reasoning: This opens an entirely untested channel in this archive — accounting conservatism rather than funding structure — with a clean mechanism: for a given reported ROA, a higher depreciation rate on non-current assets implies higher pre-accounting cash productivity and less scope for future write-downs. The denominator (assets net of current assets) makes the rate comparable across firms with different working-capital intensity, and both inputs are reported by nearly all industrial firms, so coverage should be unimpaired.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( ind_rank( ratio( oiadp, at ) ), ind_rank( ratio( dp, sub( at, act ) ) ) )

input_signals.name: OperatingFloatProfit
input_signals.hypothesis: A profitable firm whose operating cycle is largely financed by suppliers and accrued expenses runs on float: its inventory and receivables are paid for by counterparties, so growth and profits require little committed capital and cannot be interrupted by a lender's decision.
input_signals.reasoning: This is a different economic object from the archived payables-days construction: scaling operating liabilities by liquid operating assets measures what fraction of the working-capital cycle is externally floated, whereas scaling by COGS measures payment terms and is mechanically higher for low-margin, high-input businesses. That distinction is testable and matters — if the float ratio works while payables-days does not, the effect is about capital intensity of the operating cycle rather than supplier terms, which is exactly the ambiguity the previous evidence leaves open.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( ind_rank( ratio( oiadp, at ) ), ind_rank( ratio( sub( lct, dlc ), act ) ) )

input_signals.name: CashValidatedProfitVsClaims
input_signals.hypothesis: A firm should be credited only with the profitability that both its accrual accounts and its cash flow statement support, and such cash-validated earnings are most durable when the total claims eventually payable are small relative to the liquid resources already on hand.
input_signals.reasoning: The accrual-validation channel is entirely absent from the evaluated archive — every signal so far uses an accrual profitability leg — and the MIN operator implements it monotonically, demoting accrual-inflated firms to their cash profitability without the mid-distribution artifacts of an indicator. The conditioner expresses all claims per dollar of liquid assets, a claims-to-liquidity intensity that is distinct from the tested current-ratio and net-liquid-balance forms, so both legs contribute information the archive has not yet measured.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( ind_rank( ratio( min( oibdp, oancf ), at ) ), ind_rank( neg( ratio( lt, act ) ) ) )

input_signals.name: SelfFundedExpansionProfit
input_signals.expression: MUL(IND_RANK(RATIO(oiadp, at)), IND_RANK(SUB(RATIO(DELTA(re, 1), at), RATIO(DELTA(lt, 1), at))))
input_signals.hypothesis: Durable operating strength appears when the firm's own retained profits, rather than an expanding stack of external claims, fund whatever the business needs; profitability accompanied by liabilities growing faster than retained earnings is being sustained by outside capital and will not persist once that capital tightens.
input_signals.reasoning: The critique of the earlier version was correct that Δcurrent assets loads on the accrual/asset-growth anomaly, so the resilience flow is re-expressed on the financing side only: retained-earnings formation net of total claim growth, which contains no working-capital accrual component. It differs from the failed Δdebt signal because it is a *mix* variable — a firm can grow liabilities and still score well if retained earnings grow faster — making it a test of self-funding rather than of deleveraging.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( ind_rank( ratio( oiadp, at ) ), ind_rank( sub( ratio( delta( re, 1 ), at ), ratio( delta( lt, 1 ), at ) ) ) )

input_signals.name: BankedProfitTrackRecord
input_signals.hypothesis: Pretax income measures profitability after every operating and financing cost the firm actually bears, and it is credible only when it has been repeatedly banked: a steadily rising stock of retained earnings relative to assets is the accumulated, audited record that reported profits were real and were kept inside the firm.
input_signals.reasoning: Both inputs are unused in the evaluated archive — pi has never been tested as a profitability leg and re has appeared only as a static ratio to liabilities (α=1.2%) — and the trend form converts retained earnings from a stale historical stock into a measure of current earnings persistence net of distributions. This tests the "persistent" limb of the economic story through the balance sheet rather than through funding structure, giving the batch a second mechanism that does not depend on near-term claim composition.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( ind_rank( ratio( pi, at ) ), ind_rank( trend( ratio( re, at ), 3 ) ) )

input_signals.name: RisingConservatismProfit
input_signals.hypothesis: A profitable firm that raises its depreciation rate is shortening assumed asset lives and taking earnings down voluntarily — a costly, credible signal of conservative reporting — whereas a firm whose depreciation rate is falling is stretching asset lives to support reported profits that are not economically earned.
input_signals.reasoning: The level of depreciation intensity is confounded with industry technology, asset age, and goodwill-heavy denominators, but the year-on-year *change* within the same firm strips those out and isolates the discretionary accounting choice, which is the actual economic content of the conservatism hypothesis. It is therefore not a re-parameterization of the gen-4 winner but the within-firm identification of the mechanism the winner is claimed to capture.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( ind_rank( ratio( oiadp, at ) ), ind_rank( delta( ratio( dp, sub( at, act ) ), 1 ) ) )

input_signals.name: ProfitFloorConservatism
input_signals.hypothesis: Conservative depreciation matters most when the profitability it depresses is a floor rather than a peak: a firm whose *worst* return on assets in three years is high, achieved while charging aggressive depreciation, has demonstrably durable operating strength rather than a favorable single year.
input_signals.reasoning: The persistence limb of the economic story has never been properly tested in this archive — three-year averages appeared only alongside failed volatility conditioners, and the five-year minimum used in gen 0 collapsed coverage to 0.09 — so a three-year floor paired with the strongest conditioner tests whether durability adds to the conservatism effect at acceptable coverage cost. If the FMB t-statistic exceeds the 5.09 benchmark, downside profitability is the better profitability construct and should anchor the final generations.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( ind_rank( ts_min( ratio( oiadp, at ), 3 ) ), ind_rank( ratio( dp, sub( at, act ) ) ) )

input_signals.name: LeanFixedBaseProfit
input_signals.hypothesis: Profits earned on a small base of illiquid, long-lived capital reflect a business model that does not need to sink cash into replaceable hard assets to compete, so the earnings are both defensible and cheap to sustain; the same profits earned on a heavy fixed base are hostage to maintenance capital spending and to the write-down risk in that base.
input_signals.reasoning: This is the competing-hypothesis test the gen-4 result actually needs: dp/(at−act) is high both when a firm depreciates conservatively and simply when its net long-term asset base is small relative to operations, and turnover on long-term capital isolates the second reading using no income-statement item, so it cannot inherit any mechanical link with the profitability leg. If it predicts as strongly as the depreciation conditioner, the channel is capital-light operating structure rather than accounting conservatism, which changes what we should refine in the final generations.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( ind_rank( ratio( oiadp, at ) ), ind_rank( ratio( sale, sub( at, act ) ) ) )

input_signals.name: FundsValidatedProfitVsClaims
input_signals.expression: MUL(IND_RANK(RATIO(MIN(oibdp, COALESCE(oancf, ADD(ib, dp))), at)), IND_RANK(NEG(RATIO(lt, act))))
input_signals.hypothesis: A firm should be credited only with the lesser of its accrual cash profit and the cash its operations actually generated, and such validated earnings are most durable when total claims are small relative to liquid resources already on hand.
input_signals.reasoning: This keeps the cash-validation operator intact — the critique correctly noted that the previous revision discarded it — and repairs coverage instead at its true source, the availability of the cash-flow statement, by falling back to funds from operations (net income plus depreciation), the standard pre-SFAS-95 cash proxy and an economically justified missing-data convention rather than a blanket patch. If alpha holds near the 4.2% of the restricted-sample parent while coverage rises toward the archive norm, the cash-validation channel is real and not a sample artifact.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( ind_rank( ratio( min( oibdp, coalesce( oancf, add( ib, dp ) ) ), at ) ), ind_rank( neg( ratio( lt, act ) ) ) )

input_signals.name: EarnedEquityProfit
input_signals.hypothesis: The share of book equity that was earned and retained rather than contributed by investors is a lifecycle marker of proven profitability: firms whose capital base is self-generated have demonstrated repeatable earnings, while equally profitable firms whose equity is mostly paid-in are earlier-stage or post-deficit and their current returns are far less likely to persist.
input_signals.reasoning: This replaces a rediscovery of the working-capital accrual anomaly with a channel the archive has barely touched — the only retained-earnings test scaled re by liabilities, which measures solvency, whereas scaling by book equity measures the earned-versus-contributed composition of capital and is close to orthogonal to leverage and liquidity. The interaction claim is specific: current profitability should be much more persistent, and hence more underpriced, in firms whose entire equity base is the accumulated record of past profits.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( ind_rank( ratio( oiadp, at ) ), ind_rank( ratio( re, ceq ) ) )

input_signals.name: AgeAdjustedProfitConservatism
input_signals.expression: MUL(IND_RANK(RATIO(oiadp, ADD(at, TS_SUM(dp, 5)))), IND_RANK(RATIO(dp, SUB(at, act))))
input_signals.hypothesis: Book assets are reported net of accumulated depreciation, so an old asset base inflates measured return on assets; if the depreciation-intensity interaction is genuine conservatism rather than an age artifact, it must survive when profitability is measured against an approximate gross asset base that restores what has already been written off.
input_signals.reasoning: The previous version changed both legs at once and therefore identified nothing; here the conditioner is held byte-identical to the gen-4 winner and only the profitability denominator is de-biased, so the comparison is controlled and interpretable. A materially weaker result would say the archive's strongest signal is largely a stale-book-value effect, while a preserved result would justify making conservatism the anchor channel for the remaining generations — and the five-year depreciation accumulation is the only gross-asset proxy constructible from the permitted variable set.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( ind_rank( ratio( oiadp, add( at, ts_sum( dp, 5 ) ) ) ), ind_rank( ratio( dp, sub( at, act ) ) ) )

input_signals.name: CashValidatedConservatism
input_signals.expression: MUL(IND_RANK(RATIO(MIN(oiadp, SUB(COALESCE(oancf, ADD(ib, dp)), dp)), at)), IND_RANK(RATIO(dp, SUB(at, act))))
input_signals.hypothesis: The most durable earnings are those that clear two independent audits at once — the cash flow statement confirms them, and they were reported under a conservative depreciation policy that already charged the asset base heavily — so the firm's operating strength is understated on both the accrual and the capital-consumption dimension.
input_signals.reasoning: These are the archive's two best-identified channels and they are economically independent (one is a cash-versus-accrual test, the other an asset-charging policy test), so their combination is a genuine test of complementarity rather than a stack of correlated funding ranks. The cash leg is expressed on the same after-depreciation basis as the conditioner's parent (OCF less depreciation versus EBIT), preserving the negative mechanical link that made the gen-4 result conservative rather than mechanical, and the funds-from-operations fallback keeps coverage at the archive norm.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( ind_rank( ratio( min( oiadp, sub( coalesce( oancf, add( ib, dp ) ), dp ) ), at ) ), ind_rank( ratio( dp, sub( at, act ) ) ) )

input_signals.name: FundsValidatedRolloverProfit
input_signals.expression: MUL(IND_RANK(RATIO(MIN(oibdp, COALESCE(oancf, ADD(ib, dp))), at)), IND_RANK(NEG(RATIO(dlc, act))))
input_signals.hypothesis: Cash-validated operating profitability and freedom from callable near-term debt are separate defences against profit reversal — one against accounting overstatement, the other against forced retrenchment — and firms possessing both should command the largest premium.
input_signals.reasoning: The archive's two highest alphas (4.2% each) come from these ingredients used separately with different partners, and their parents have distinctly different risk profiles (Sharpe 0.19 versus 0.25), which suggests imperfect correlation and therefore scope for genuine reinforcement rather than redundancy. As a consolidation cell this is directly actionable: if alpha rises materially above 4.2% with a t-statistic above 4, the final recommended signal should pair cash validation with maturity risk rather than choose between them.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( ind_rank( ratio( min( oibdp, coalesce( oancf, add( ib, dp ) ) ), at ) ), ind_rank( neg( ratio( dlc, act ) ) ) )

input_signals.name: OperatingCycleStabilityProfit
input_signals.hypothesis: A profitable firm whose operating cycle is stable — receivables and inventory holding a constant relation to sales year after year — has predictable demand, disciplined credit terms, and no need for emergency financing, whereas a swinging cycle reveals demand shocks or channel stuffing that make current profitability unreliable.
input_signals.reasoning: The archive has tested stability only on financing variables (leverage volatility failed, short-term-debt volatility worked at α = 3.1%, t = 2.8), never on the operating side, so this asks whether the stability limb of the economic story runs through operations rather than through funding. It also replaces a measurement-noise tweak with a distinct economic quantity: the variability of working-capital intensity is close to orthogonal to the level effects already documented, and it uses only universally reported items so coverage should hold near the archive norm.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( ind_rank( ratio( oiadp, at ) ), ind_rank( neg( vol( ratio( act, sale ), 3 ) ) ) )

input_signals.name: QualityIndexProfit
input_signals.expression: MUL(IND_RANK(RATIO(oiadp, at)), IND_RANK(SUMRANK(RATIO(dp, SUB(at, act)), NEG(RATIO(dlc, act)))))
input_signals.hypothesis: Durable operating strength requires quality on two economically independent dimensions — earnings reported under a conservative capital-charging policy, and an absence of callable claims against liquid resources — so profitability should be conditioned on a two-dimensional quality index rather than on either dimension alone.
input_signals.reasoning: This is the consolidation the evidence now supports: the two conditioners come from different data domains (income-statement accounting policy versus balance-sheet maturity structure) and have complementary statistical profiles, one carrying the slope and Sharpe, the other the alpha. Using SUMRANK to build the index preserves cross-sectional dispersion — the specific defect that made earlier three-way rank *products* shrink the spread — so this tests complementarity without the compression that doomed the gen-2 triple screen.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( ind_rank( ratio( oiadp, at ) ), ind_rank( sumrank( ratio( dp, sub( at, act ) ), neg( ratio( dlc, act ) ) ) ) )

input_signals.name: IntangibleProfitConservatism
input_signals.expression: MUL(IND_RANK(RATIO(ADD(oiadp, COALESCE(xrd, 0)), at)), IND_RANK(RATIO(dp, SUB(at, act))))
input_signals.hypothesis: Adding back expensed R&D restores true operating profitability, and pairing that restored measure with a conservative depreciation policy identifies firms whose economic earnings exceed reported earnings on both the intangible and the tangible dimension.
input_signals.reasoning: This is one of the two untested cells of the profitability-leg × conditioner factorial that must be filled before a final recommendation, and it is not a foregone conclusion: R&D-intensive firms typically report *low* depreciation rates, so the two legs select partly opposing populations and the interaction could easily be weaker than either parent. Whichever way it resolves, it tells us whether the final signal should use restored or reported profitability alongside the conservatism conditioner.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( ind_rank( ratio( add( oiadp, coalesce( xrd, 0 ) ), at ) ), ind_rank( ratio( dp, sub( at, act ) ) ) )

input_signals.name: IntangibleProfitRollover
input_signals.hypothesis: R&D-restored profitability is the most complete measure of operating strength, and it is most durable in firms with no callable debt, because rollover pressure forces exactly the discretionary investment cuts that destroy an intangible-based competitive position.
input_signals.reasoning: This is the second missing factorial cell and pairs the archive's highest-alpha profitability leg (4.1%, ls_talpha 4.07 with a liquidity conditioner) with its highest-alpha conditioner (4.2%, t 3.79 with plain ROA), so it is the single most likely candidate to exceed the 4.2% alpha ceiling that every construction has hit so far. Evaluated alongside Signal 4 it also separates whether the R&D add-back interacts with funding safety or with accounting conservatism, which the two parents cannot distinguish.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( ind_rank( ratio( add( oiadp, coalesce( xrd, 0 ) ), at ) ), ind_rank( neg( ratio( dlc, act ) ) ) )

input_signals.name: FragileEarningsRollover
input_signals.hypothesis: Callable debt is dangerous precisely when operating results are unpredictable: a firm with steady returns can always refinance, and a firm with volatile returns can survive a bad year if nothing is due, but the combination of earnings instability and maturing claims is what forces distressed retrenchment and destroys profitability.
input_signals.reasoning: Every archive signal conditions the *level* of profitability, never its stability, on funding structure, yet the economic story's "stable" limb predicts an interaction specifically between second-moment earnings risk and callable claims — a joint-fragility mechanism rather than two additive quality screens. It is also a useful diagnostic for the final generations: if it performs comparably to level-based pairings, the premium is compensation for distress-state risk, whereas if it fails, the level of operating strength is what the market misprices.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( ind_rank( neg( vol( ratio( oiadp, at ), 3 ) ) ), ind_rank( neg( ratio( dlc, act ) ) ) )

input_signals.name: DualChargeConservatismProfit
input_signals.expression: MUL(IND_RANK(RATIO(oiadp, at)), IND_RANK(SUMRANK(RATIO(dp, SUB(at, act)), RATIO(COALESCE(xrd, 0), at))))
input_signals.hypothesis: Conservative reporting depresses earnings through two independent charges — fast write-down of tangible capital and outright expensing of intangible investment — and a firm that remains highly profitable while making both charges has the most deeply understated operating strength.
input_signals.reasoning: The critique of the raw sum was correct: adding R&D dollars to depreciation over a small long-term-asset base lets an R&D/PPE explosion dominate, so each charge is now measured as a rate on an appropriate base and combined through SUMRANK, which ranks the two components separately and is immune to their scale difference. This also distinguishes the proposal from the published R&D-intensity effect, because a firm scores highly only by being conservative on *both* dimensions, and the archive has never tested R&D intensity as a conditioner — only as an add-back inside the profitability leg.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( ind_rank( ratio( oiadp, at ) ), ind_rank( sumrank( ratio( dp, sub( at, act ) ), ratio( coalesce( xrd, 0 ), at ) ) ) )

input_signals.name: MaturityMismatchProfit
input_signals.hypothesis: The classic financing error is funding long-lived, illiquid assets with debt that must be renegotiated every year; profitability generated on a fixed asset base carrying heavy short-maturity funding is hostage to the credit cycle, whereas the same profitability with maturity-matched funding is durable.
input_signals.reasoning: This replaces a near-collinear reparameterization with a genuinely different object: dlc/act asks whether liquid resources cover maturing claims, while dlc/(at−act) asks whether the *illiquid* asset base is being financed at the wrong maturity, and the two denominators are drawn from disjoint parts of the balance sheet so the measures are far from collinear. It also completes the maturity-structure map alongside the already-tested dlc/lt and the now-rejected dltt/act, telling us whether the callability premium reflects a coverage shortfall or an asset-liability duration mismatch.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( ind_rank( ratio( oiadp, at ) ), ind_rank( neg( ratio( dlc, sub( at, act ) ) ) ) )

input_signals.name: CapitalizedRnDProfitRollover
input_signals.expression: MUL(IND_RANK(RATIO(ADD(oiadp, COALESCE(xrd, 0)), ADD(at, TS_SUM(COALESCE(xrd, 0), 5)))), IND_RANK(NEG(RATIO(dlc, act))))
input_signals.hypothesis: If expensed R&D is genuinely investment, it belongs on both sides of the profitability ratio: the income statement understates earnings by the current year's spend and the balance sheet understates capital by the accumulated knowledge stock, so a fully capitalized return on assets is the correct measure of durable operating strength.
input_signals.reasoning: The archive's highest-alpha signal adds R&D back only to the numerator, which mechanically inflates measured returns for research-intensive firms and leaves open whether the premium reflects true productivity or a denominator omission — capitalizing the five-year knowledge stock removes that asymmetry. This is a substantive measurement correction rather than a recombination, and it is the cleanest available test of why the R&D-restored leg outperforms; its coverage cost from the five-year accumulation should be read against the archive norm.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( ind_rank( ratio( add( oiadp, coalesce( xrd, 0 ) ), add( at, ts_sum( coalesce( xrd, 0 ), 5 ) ) ) ), ind_rank( neg( ratio( dlc, act ) ) ) )

input_signals.name: StableEarningsConservatism
input_signals.hypothesis: Conservative capital charging is most informative for firms whose operating returns are steady: a stable earnings stream reported under aggressive depreciation is understated economic income that will keep repeating, whereas volatile earnings tell us little about the policy's meaning.
input_signals.reasoning: The second-moment channel proved real when paired with callable debt (α 2.9%, t 3.0), and this fills the remaining cell of the {level, stability} × {conservatism, callability} design, pairing earnings stability with the archive's most powerful conditioner. It also serves as a discriminating test of the mispricing story: if stability substitutes for the profitability level without loss, the premium is about predictability of understated earnings rather than about the level of operating strength.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( ind_rank( neg( vol( ratio( oiadp, at ), 3 ) ) ), ind_rank( ratio( dp, sub( at, act ) ) ) )

input_signals.name: TaxValidatedProfitRollover
input_signals.hypothesis: Tax expense is the one earnings validation a firm pays real money for: profits that generate a large tax charge relative to assets have been asserted to the tax authority as well as to investors, so they are far harder to manufacture than accrual profits, and such validated earnings are durable when no callable debt threatens the business.
input_signals.reasoning: Cash-flow validation was tested twice and added nothing beyond the underlying profitability (α fell from 4.2% to 3.8% when paired with the rollover conditioner), so the natural next validation channel is the book-tax dimension, which no archive signal has touched and which is orthogonal to the operating-cash-flow test because it screens for non-recurring, non-taxable, and accounting-only income. Pretax income and bottom-line income are both universally reported, so this carries no coverage cost and gives the profitability leg a genuinely different economic definition rather than a re-scaling.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( ind_rank( ratio( sub( pi, ib ), at ) ), ind_rank( neg( ratio( dlc, act ) ) ) )

input_signals.name: ReserveConservatismProfit
input_signals.expression: MUL(IND_RANK(RATIO(ADD(oiadp, COALESCE(xrd, 0)), at)), IND_RANK(RATIO(SUB(SUB(lt, dltt), lct), at)))
input_signals.hypothesis: Liabilities that are neither long-term debt nor current obligations are largely deferred taxes, pension and warranty reserves, and other provisions — balance-sheet conservatism in recognizing future costs early — so a highly profitable firm carrying large reserves has understated both its earnings and its equity and is reporting from a position of strength.
input_signals.reasoning: This moves the conservatism mechanism, which the archive has established only on the income statement through depreciation policy, to the liability side of the balance sheet where it has never been measured, and the residual-liability construction uses only quality-exclusive items so it cannot be a restatement of any tested leverage or liquidity ratio. It is also economically linked to the depreciation finding in a testable way — accelerated tax depreciation is the main source of deferred tax liabilities — so a positive result would corroborate the conservatism interpretation from an independent data domain.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( ind_rank( ratio( add( oiadp, coalesce( xrd, 0 ) ), at ) ), ind_rank( ratio( sub( sub( lt, dltt ), lct ), at ) ) )

input_signals.name: FloorRestoredProfitConservatism
input_signals.expression: MUL(IND_RANK(TS_MIN(RATIO(ADD(oiadp, COALESCE(xrd, 0)), at), 3)), IND_RANK(RATIO(dp, SUB(at, act))))
input_signals.hypothesis: The profitability that earns a quality premium is the level sustained in the worst of the last three years; a three-year floor on intangible-restored returns, reported under conservative depreciation, identifies operating strength that has already been tested by a downturn.
input_signals.reasoning: The critique is accepted: this now varies exactly one element — TS_MIN — against the standing archive baseline IntangibleProfitConservatism (fmb 6.19, α 3.9%, t 3.51), holding the conditioner and the profitability definition fixed, so any change in alpha or slope is attributable to the floor construction alone. That attribution matters for the final generation because the floor previously raised the slope but cost alpha when applied to plain ROA, and we need to know whether it does the same to the restored leg before choosing the final form.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( ind_rank( ts_min( ratio( add( oiadp, coalesce( xrd, 0 ) ), at ), 3 ) ), ind_rank( ratio( dp, sub( at, act ) ) ) )

input_signals.name: PolicyRateConservatismProfit
input_signals.expression: MUL(IND_RANK(RATIO(ADD(oiadp, COALESCE(xrd, 0)), at)), IND_RANK(RATIO(dp, ADD(SUB(at, act), TS_SUM(dp, 5)))))
input_signals.hypothesis: Depreciation divided by *net* long-term assets rises mechanically as an asset base ages, conflating a firm's useful-life policy with the vintage of its equipment; measured against an estimated *gross* base it isolates the deliberate policy choice, which is the conservatism the hypothesis is actually about.
input_signals.reasoning: This is the measurement correction the critic has flagged since gen 4 — asset-age contamination of dp/(at−act) — and gen 5 only de-biased the profitability denominator, never the conditioner itself, so the question remains open and is central to interpreting the archive's strongest channel. If the policy rate performs as well or better, the finding is genuinely about conservative reporting and generalizes; if it degrades materially, the premium is an asset-age/stale-book-value effect and the final signal should say so rather than claim conservatism.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( ind_rank( ratio( add( oiadp, coalesce( xrd, 0 ) ), at ) ), ind_rank( ratio( dp, add( sub( at, act ), ts_sum( dp, 5 ) ) ) ) )

input_signals.name: AmortizedRnDProfitRollover
input_signals.expression: MUL(IND_RANK(RATIO(SUB(ADD(oiadp, COALESCE(xrd, 0)), MA(COALESCE(xrd, 0), 5)), ADD(at, TS_SUM(COALESCE(xrd, 0), 5)))), IND_RANK(NEG(RATIO(dlc, act))))
input_signals.hypothesis: If R&D is capitalized it must also be amortized: economic operating profit equals reported EBIT plus the current year's R&D spend less the periodic write-off of the accumulated knowledge stock, measured against an asset base that includes that stock, and this properly specified return is what should interact with freedom from callable debt.
input_signals.reasoning: This repairs the internal inconsistency the critic identified in CapitalizedRnDProfitRollover, which added back the full current spend while charging no amortization against the capitalized stock, thereby flattering steady-state R&D spenders; the five-year moving average of R&D is exactly the straight-line amortization of a five-year knowledge stock, so the numerator and denominator are now consistent. Since that half-specified version already reached α 4.7% (t 4.22), the corrected version isolates whether the intangible premium reflects genuine productivity net of intangible capital consumption.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( ind_rank( ratio( sub( add( oiadp, coalesce( xrd, 0 ) ), ma( coalesce( xrd, 0 ), 5 ) ), add( at, ts_sum( coalesce( xrd, 0 ), 5 ) ) ) ), ind_rank( neg( ratio( dlc, act ) ) ) )

input_signals.name: TaxValidatedConservatism
input_signals.expression: MUL(IND_RANK(RATIO(SUB(pi, ib), at)), IND_RANK(RATIO(dp, ADD(SUB(at, act), TS_SUM(dp, 5)))))
input_signals.hypothesis: Two independent hard validations of earnings coincide here: a large tax charge proves profits were asserted to the tax authority, and a conservative book depreciation policy proves they were reported after a heavy capital charge, so firms scoring on both have operating strength that neither accounting discretion nor selective disclosure could manufacture.
input_signals.reasoning: The tax channel is new to the archive and worked modestly with the funding conditioner (α 2.6%, t 2.4), but it should interact far more informatively with conservatism, since heavy book depreciation ordinarily *reduces* taxable-income conformity — a firm that charges book depreciation aggressively and still pays substantial tax is unusually credible. This is the only cell that pairs two validation mechanisms rather than a validation with a balance-sheet risk measure.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( ind_rank( ratio( sub( pi, ib ), at ) ), ind_rank( ratio( dp, add( sub( at, act ), ts_sum( dp, 5 ) ) ) ) )

input_signals.name: CredibleDepreciationPolicyProfit
input_signals.expression: MUL(IND_RANK(RATIO(ADD(oiadp, COALESCE(xrd, 0)), at)), IND_RANK(NEG(VOL(RATIO(dp, SUB(at, act)), 3))))
input_signals.hypothesis: A depreciation rate that stays constant year after year reflects a stable, non-discretionary useful-life policy, whereas a rate that jumps around signals write-off timing, impairment management, or acquisition-driven restatement of the asset base — so profitability reported under a *credible* policy is more trustworthy than profitability reported under a shifting one.
input_signals.reasoning: Every conservatism test so far has been about the level or the direction of the depreciation rate; its stability is a different economic object — reporting credibility rather than reporting conservatism — and it directly addresses the measurement-noise concern the critic raised about capex timing and acquisitions contaminating the level. As the exploratory slot it is also diagnostic for interpretation: if credibility predicts independently of level, the channel is about the trustworthiness of reported earnings rather than about understatement per se.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( ind_rank( ratio( add( oiadp, coalesce( xrd, 0 ) ), at ) ), ind_rank( neg( vol( ratio( dp, sub( at, act ) ), 3 ) ) ) )

input_signals.name: FreeOperatingProfitRollover
input_signals.expression: MUL(IND_RANK(RATIO(SUB(ADD(oiadp, dp), DELTA(SUB(at, act), 1)), at)), IND_RANK(NEG(RATIO(dlc, act))))
input_signals.hypothesis: The profit an owner can actually withdraw is cash operating income less the net investment required to keep the long-lived asset base intact, so EBITDA minus the change in net long-term assets is the true distributable operating return; such genuinely free profitability is durable when no callable debt has a prior claim on the firm's liquid resources.
input_signals.reasoning: This replaces an index recombination with a new profitability construct that unifies the archive's two accounting findings economically rather than statistically — firms scoring highly are exactly those that charge heavy depreciation while not having to spend it back, which is what the conservatism channel has been capturing indirectly through dp/(at−act). Pairing it with the highest-alpha conditioner keeps the funding channel intact without SUMRANK dilution, and every input is universally reported so coverage should match the archive norm.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( ind_rank( ratio( sub( add( oiadp, dp ), delta( sub( at, act ), 1 ) ), at ) ), ind_rank( neg( ratio( dlc, act ) ) ) )

input_signals.name: GrossInvestedCapitalProfitRollover
input_signals.expression: MUL(IND_RANK(RATIO(ADD(oiadp, COALESCE(xrd, 0)), ADD(ADD(at, TS_SUM(dp, 5)), TS_SUM(COALESCE(xrd, 0), 5)))), IND_RANK(NEG(RATIO(dlc, act))))
input_signals.hypothesis: Total invested capital is reported assets plus what accounting has removed from them — accumulated depreciation on tangible assets and the entire expensed intangible stock — so return on gross invested capital is the only profitability measure comparable across firms of different asset age and different intangible intensity, and it is durable when callable claims are absent.
input_signals.reasoning: The critique was correct that the previous denominator restored only the intangible omission, never accumulated depreciation, so the "consistent invested capital" claim was not what the expression computed; both write-backs are now applied, making the measure internally coherent for the first time in the archive. Pairing it with the callable-debt conditioner rather than with the depreciation conditioner also removes the mechanical entanglement between a depreciation-adjusted denominator and a depreciation-rate conditioner, so the test cleanly asks whether true capital productivity, not accounting artifact, drives the interaction.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( ind_rank( ratio( add( oiadp, coalesce( xrd, 0 ) ), add( add( at, ts_sum( dp, 5 ) ), ts_sum( coalesce( xrd, 0 ), 5 ) ) ) ), ind_rank( neg( ratio( dlc, act ) ) ) )

input_signals.name: StressStateProfitFunding
input_signals.hypothesis: A firm's durability should be judged in its bad state, not its average one: the lowest restored return it earned in three years paired with the highest short-term-debt exposure it carried over the same window describes how the business looks when operations and funding are simultaneously at their worst.
input_signals.reasoning: This is not a single-component swap but a change in the evaluation state — both legs are moved from their central tendency to their adverse extreme, testing the risk-based reading of the entire archive, namely that the premium compensates for how bad the joint profitability-and-funding state can get rather than for average characteristics. The two ingredients performed well individually with conventional partners (floor profitability fmb 6.30, Sharpe 0.461; peak rollover exposure α 3.4%), yet their worst-state pairing has never been run, and it is the cleanest available discrimination between distress-risk compensation and mispricing of understated earnings.
